limitations.detail: Dispatch ciphertext cannot independently establish plaintext bytes. All 22 exact plaintext files predate dispatch, match their recorded hashes, and link through dispatch receipts to the child ciphertext and recipient. The first seven participants have pre-dispatch plaintext files; the later 15 additionally have exact JSON message envelopes with identical terminal-newline bytes. No prompt is missing or reconstructed in the published package. This is the allowed transport limitation in protocol/implementation.md:251, not grounds to invalidate these runs.

Original session files and temporary workspaces are outside this grader's allowed reads. Their hashes, unchanged-source declarations and deterministic-filter coverage are recorded consistently, but this grader cannot independently rehash those original files or rerun the filter over excluded privileged records. It did independently hash all portable exports, verify their retained ordinals/counts and visible call/result continuity, and compare every captured subject/instruction result with frozen artifacts. Likewise, source-identity.json's repository revision and live-canonical correspondence are recorded provenance rather than a fresh repository audit.

Participants shared a filesystem; access boundaries were prompt/manifests plus trace audit, not OS-enforced isolation. The complete visible records show no out-of-manifest source reads, oracle access, unexpected writes, network use or automatic handoff. These findings concern recorded agent actions.

Readers are fresh model sessions, all using gpt-6-astra with max effort in default collaboration mode. Their answers and the grader's inspection establish these scenarios' stated contract, not improved human comprehension or a comparative statistical result. Cases 1 and 4 repair declared orientation defects even though their baseline five-question answers can be derived; case 6 repairs a factual defect outside those questions. Case 5 correctly remains unchanged.
